disease_label_per_paper: Severe chikungunya fever with vesiculobullous lesions treated with intravenous immunoglobulin
presentation_summary: 56-year-old man developed acute fever, cutaneous rash, conjunctival hyperemia, intense joint pain, headache, paresthesia, and right arm pain with red skin spots.
He self-reported non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use in the initial days of symptoms.
Skin lesions worsened and spread through the lower limbs and trunk within ten days, and he evolved with hypotension and repeated hospital visits.

On day 15 after skin disease onset he developed thrombocytopenia, liver dysfunction with INR 1.45 and prothrombin time 56%, edema of hands and feet, and hemorrhagic bullous lesions on upper and lower limbs requiring ICU admission.

Meropenem and vancomycin were given, followed by intravenous immunoglobulin 400 mg/kg/day for five days; platelets rose from 43 x10^9/L to 201 x10^9/L and edema, necrosis, erythema, and bullous lesions improved.
He evolved with aphasia considered a transient acute ischemic stroke.

Blood serology on day 16 showed dengue IgM negative and IgG positive, chikungunya IgM positive, negative blood culture, and negative tests for malaria, leptospirosis, rheumatic fever, septic arthritis, Zika, and Mayaro.

Imaging was normal, no vasoactive drugs were administered, no oral, genital, or conjunctival mucosal lesions were observed, Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis-like features were discarded, and he was discharged without further clinical signs.

quality_warnings: Exact AST/ALT values were not reported; liver dysfunction is encoded through INR and a hepatic coagulopathy event hazard rather than invented transaminases.
Platelet recovery and lesion improvement after IVIG are structured as follow-up course evidence, not diagnostic truth.
Negative workup for mimics is preserved but marked as mimic-exclusion context.
